blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Filipino fisherfolk are experiencing skin problems, heat-related illnesses and reduced fishing hours as extreme heat affects their work at sea, prompting an environmental group to urge the government to provide alternative livelihoods and stronger social protection as a very strong El Niño persists in the Pacific. El Niño is a climate phenomenon marked by above-normal sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean, which can influence rainfall and temperature patterns in different parts of the world.
